messages.author: e5f9ceca0d85898b
messages.subject: unwanted horizontal lines on map
parts:
I'm mapping points in various areas of the world. However, when I
narrow the axis ranges of the map to better frame the data, unwanted
horizontal lines appear that look like borders. The number and
location of these lines varies, depending on the global region and lat/
long limits. For example the second of the two maps below has false
lines near the top and bottom:

library(ggplot2)
library ("maps")

df<-data.frame(x=c(145:150), y=c(45:50))
map1 <- ggplot(data = df, (aes(x=x, y=y)))
map1 <- map1 + geom_point(size=2, colour="blue")
map1 <- map1 + borders ("world", size = 0.2, colour = "grey70")

#borders OK
map1 + coord_map(xlim = c(-180,180), ylim = c(-50, 100))

#borders plus unwanted horizontal lines
map1 + coord_map(xlim = c(100,180), ylim = c(-10, 71))

Q1) How can I eliminate these unwanted lines?

Somewhat unrelated questions about mapping:
Q2) For data that span the antimeridian, how can I center the map
around long=180, rather than have to display the entire world map?
Q3) I'm new to ggplot and R. I've read the ggplot2 book and started
climbing its learning curve. Is there a way to use ggplot2 to plot
data onto GoogleEarth base images?

Many thanks in advance,
Stephen

On Thu, Mar 8, 2012 at 6:59 PM, Stephen <yeze...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm mapping points in various areas of the world. However, when I
> narrow the axis ranges of the map to better frame the data, unwanted
> horizontal lines appear that look like borders. The number and
> location of these lines varies, depending on the global region and lat/
> long limits. For example the second of the two maps below has false
> lines near the top and bottom:
>
> library(ggplot2)
> library ("maps")
>
> df<-data.frame(x=c(145:150), y=c(45:50))
> map1 <- ggplot(data = df, (aes(x=x, y=y)))
> map1 <- map1 + geom_point(size=2, colour="blue")
> map1 <- map1 + borders ("world", size = 0.2, colour = "grey70")
>
> #borders OK
> map1 + coord_map(xlim = c(-180,180), ylim = c(-50, 100))
>
> #borders plus unwanted horizontal lines
> map1 + coord_map(xlim = c(100,180), ylim = c(-10, 71))
>
> Q1) How can I eliminate these unwanted lines?

This is unfortunately a long standing bug with the map coordinate
system. Winston is currently battling with similar issues for polar
coordinates, so maybe once he's solved those he might be able to look
into these problems (plus I think he will soon be writing a spatial
chapter for his book).

> Somewhat unrelated questions about mapping:
> Q2) For data that span the antimeridian, how can I center the map
> around long=180, rather than have to display the entire world map?
You can't do that by setting xlim and ylim?

> Q3) I'm new to ggplot and R. I've read the ggplot2 book and started
> climbing its learning curve. Is there a way to use ggplot2 to plot
> data onto GoogleEarth base images?

Yes, see the ggmap package.

Hadley
